problem_statement: os_mbuf_pack_chains must concatenate two mbuf chains, repack data so all but the final mbuf are full, and free mbufs emptied by packing.

simulator_fixture_proof.purpose: Pass the already allocated native stack's scaled size to os_task_init; identical in all phases.

verification.reason: The original statement is too terse to specify the public API and the edge-case behaviours required by the hidden test, but these can be added without describing the implementation.

problems.detail: The statement names os_mbuf_pack_chains but does not give its parameter types, return type, or that it is a public mbuf API; the hidden test calls os_mbuf_pack_chains(m1, m2) and uses the returned os_mbuf *.

The statement omits required observable behaviours checked by the hidden test: m2 may be NULL while m1 is still repacked; packet headers in m1 are retained and their packet length is updated; packet headers in m2 are discarded; zero-length mbufs are removed/freed; no new mbufs are allocated; all non-final mbufs must be full; om_data must have no leading space; om_len/om_data/om_pkthdr_len must reflect the packed result.
The hidden test relies on the public prototype being available; the statement does not state the header or declaration form.

problem_statement_fixed: os_mbuf_pack_chains must concatenate two mbuf chains, repack data so all but the final mbuf are full, and free mbufs emptied by packing. The public function has the signature struct os_mbuf *os_mbuf_pack_chains(struct os_mbuf *m1, struct os_mbuf *m2). It packs the chains into a single chain based on m1. If m2 is NULL, the function must still compact m1 and return it. If m2 is non-NULL, the mbufs of m2 are appended after m1, preserving data content and order. If m1 is a packet-header mbuf, the result retains m1's packet header and updates its packet length to include the appended data; any packet header on m2 is discarded. No mbufs are allocated; only mbufs from the supplied chains are used. The resulting chain must contain no leading space in any mbuf: each mbuf's om_data must point to the start of its usable data area, after any packet-header length if the mbuf is a packet-header mbuf. Every mbuf except the last must be full to the end of its usable databuf; the last mbuf may be partially full. Mbufs that become empty after their data is copied into preceding mbufs must be freed, and the resulting chain must contain no zero-length mbufs.
